exams.syllabus: ABRSM Singing / Singing for Musical Theatre Practical Grades. Lists read from the board's official syllabus PDF.
comps: Marks

150 total: three accompanied songs 30 each (90), unaccompanied song 21, sight-singing 21, aural tests 18. Distinction 130-150, Merit 120-129, Pass 100-119 (a pass in each component is not required). UCAS points G6/G7/G8 (Pass/Merit/Distinction): 8/10/12, 12/14/16, 18/24/30.
Choosing pieces

Three accompanied songs from memory, one from each of Lists A, B and C, with live piano accompaniment (no recorded accompaniment; candidate cannot accompany themselves). One unaccompanied song from memory chosen from songs marked as eligible in any list (cannot also be sung accompanied; own choice of section, listed cuts need not be observed). Maximum one 'long' song among the accompanied songs. Any voice and key at G1-7; at G8 up to a tone above/below published keys. Songs complete including repeats unless the listing gives cuts; any edition may be used; any gender; original language or singing translation allowed. Song lists are the same as for Singing for Musical Theatre Performance Grades.
Digital exams

Song lists are shared with the Performance Grades qualification (candidates taking both at the same grade are advised to prepare different songs); the text mentions face-to-face and digital exams generally but gives no separate digital requirements.
sections: Scales & technical work

No scales, arpeggios or technical work. Components: three accompanied songs, one unaccompanied song (1-2 min section, G1-5; 1-3 min, G6-8, chosen from songs marked as eligible), sight-singing, aural tests.
Sight-reading

Sight-singing (accompanied by examiner at piano, 30 seconds preparation): 6 bars (2-bar piano intro + 4 bars vocal), 4/4; C, G, F majors; up to a 6th within C4-D5 (bass clef C3-D4); repeated notes, diatonic major/minor 2nds, rising/falling minor 3rds within tonic chord; cresc./dim. hairpins; piano doubles vocal line, intro same as final bars; English words optional (any vowel or sol-fa allowed).
Aural & other tests

a) clap the pulse and say if two or three time; b) sing as echoes three 2-bar phrases (major key, tonic-mediant); c) identify where a pitch change occurs in a 2-bar phrase (near beginning/end); d) answer questions on two features (dynamics; articulation).

Choosing pieces

Three accompanied songs from memory, one from each of Lists A, B and C, with live piano accompaniment (no recorded accompaniment; candidate cannot accompany themselves). One unaccompanied song from memory chosen from songs marked as eligible in any list (cannot also be sung accompanied; own choice of section, listed cuts need not be observed). Maximum one 'long' song among the accompanied songs. Any voice and key at G1-7; at G8 up to a tone above/below published keys. Songs complete including repeats unless the listing gives cuts; any edition may be used; any gender; original language or singing translation allowed. sections: Scales & technical work

Aural & other tests
a) clap pulse, two or three time; b) echo three 2-bar phrases (major, tonic-dominant range); c) identify a pitch or rhythm change in a 2-bar phrase; d) two features (dynamics or articulation; tempo).

exams.syllabus: ABRSM Singing / Singing for Musical Theatre Practical Grades. Lists read from the board's official syllabus PDF.
comps: Marks

150 total: three accompanied songs 30 each (90), unaccompanied song 21, sight-singing 21, aural tests 18. Distinction 130-150, Merit 120-129, Pass 100-119 (a pass in each component is not required). UCAS points G6/G7/G8 (Pass/Merit/Distinction): 8/10/12, 12/14/16, 18/24/30.
Choosing pieces

Three accompanied songs from memory, one from each of Lists A, B and C, with live piano accompaniment (no recorded accompaniment; candidate cannot accompany themselves). One unaccompanied song from memory chosen from songs marked as eligible in any list (cannot also be sung accompanied; own choice of section, listed cuts need not be observed). Maximum one 'long' song among the accompanied songs. Any voice and key at G1-7; at G8 up to a tone above/below published keys. Songs complete including repeats unless the listing gives cuts; any edition may be used; any gender; original language or singing translation allowed. Song lists are the same as for Singing for Musical Theatre Performance Grades.
Digital exams

Song lists are shared with the Performance Grades qualification (candidates taking both at the same grade are advised to prepare different songs); the text mentions face-to-face and digital exams generally but gives no separate digital requirements.
sections: Scales & technical work

No scales, arpeggios or technical work. Components: three accompanied songs, one unaccompanied song (1-2 min section, G1-5; 1-3 min, G6-8, chosen from songs marked as eligible), sight-singing, aural tests.
Sight-reading

Sight-singing (accompanied by examiner at piano, 30 seconds preparation): 10-14 bars (intro 2 or 4, vocal 8-10); adds A and E-flat majors; about an octave within B-flat3-D5; rising and falling perfect 4ths; anacrusis; accidentals in minor keys only; intro not always same as final bars.
Aural & other tests

a) sing from memory a melody (octave range, up to 3 sharps/flats) played twice; b) sing four major/perfect intervals up to a 5th above a given note; c) (i) two features of a played piece (dynamics, articulation, tempo or tonality; rhythm) and (ii) clap on a requested beat (not the first) of the bar.

exams.syllabus: ABRSM Singing / Singing for Musical Theatre Practical Grades. Lists read from the board's official syllabus PDF.
comps: Marks

150 total: three accompanied songs 30 each (90), unaccompanied song 21, sight-singing 21, aural tests 18. Distinction 130-150, Merit 120-129, Pass 100-119 (a pass in each component is not required). UCAS points G6/G7/G8 (Pass/Merit/Distinction): 8/10/12, 12/14/16, 18/24/30.
Choosing pieces

Three accompanied songs from memory, one from each of Lists A, B and C, with live piano accompaniment (no recorded accompaniment; candidate cannot accompany themselves). One unaccompanied song from memory chosen from songs marked as eligible in any list (cannot also be sung accompanied; own choice of section, listed cuts need not be observed). Maximum one 'long' song among the accompanied songs. Any voice and key at G1-7; at G8 up to a tone above/below published keys. Songs complete including repeats unless the listing gives cuts; any edition may be used; any gender; original language or singing translation allowed. Song lists are the same as for Singing for Musical Theatre Performance Grades.
Digital exams

Song lists are shared with the Performance Grades qualification (candidates taking both at the same grade are advised to prepare different songs); the text mentions face-to-face and digital exams generally but gives no separate digital requirements.
sections: Scales & technical work

No scales, arpeggios or technical work. Components: three accompanied songs, one unaccompanied song (1-2 min section, G1-5; 1-3 min, G6-8, chosen from songs marked as eligible), sight-singing, aural tests.
Sight-reading

Sight-singing (accompanied by examiner at piano, 30 seconds preparation): As Grade 4 plus G minor (range B-flat2-D4 in bass clef version) and perfect 5ths; accompaniments fuller, occasionally supporting the vocal line.
Aural & other tests

a) sing back a melody played twice (as G4); b) sing four major/perfect intervals up to a 7th above a given note; c) (i) two features (dynamics, articulation, tempo, tonality or rhythm; character) and (ii) clap on a requested quaver ('and' of a beat) while first four bars replayed.

150 total: three accompanied songs 30 each (90), unaccompanied song 21, sight-singing 21, aural tests 18. Distinction 130-150, Merit 120-129, Pass 100-119 (a pass in each component is not required). UCAS points G6/G7/G8 (Pass/Merit/Distinction): 8/10/12, 12/14/16, 18/24/30.
Choosing pieces

Three accompanied songs from memory, one from each of Lists A, B and C, with live piano accompaniment (no recorded accompaniment; candidate cannot accompany themselves). One unaccompanied song from memory chosen from songs marked as eligible in any list (cannot also be sung accompanied; own choice of section, listed cuts need not be observed). Maximum one 'long' song among the accompanied songs. Any voice and key at G1-7; at G8 up to a tone above/below published keys. Songs complete including repeats unless the listing gives cuts; any edition may be used; any gender; original language or singing translation allowed. Song lists are the same as for Singing for Musical Theatre Performance Grades.
Before you enter
Grade 5 Music Theory (or Practical Musicianship Grade 5, or Grade 5 on a Practical Grades solo jazz instrument, or accepted alternative) required before entering Grade 6, 7 or 8. No Initial Grade.
Digital exams

Song lists are shared with the Performance Grades qualification (candidates taking both at the same grade are advised to prepare different songs); the text mentions face-to-face and digital exams generally but gives no separate digital requirements.
sections: Scales & technical work

No scales, arpeggios or technical work. Components: three accompanied songs, one unaccompanied song (1-2 min section, G1-5; 1-3 min, G6-8, chosen from songs marked as eligible), sight-singing, aural tests.
Sight-reading

Sight-singing (accompanied by examiner at piano, 30 seconds preparation): c. 10-16 bars (intro 2 or 4, vocal 8-12), 6/8 introduced; keys incl. B, F-sharp and C minors; major/minor 6ths and minor 7ths; occasional chromatic notes; vocal line increasingly independent of piano.
Aural & other tests

a) sing from memory the upper part of a two-part phrase played twice; b) sing four major/minor/perfect intervals up to a 7th above a given note; c) identify a note sung as part of a chord (root/3rd/5th), then in a different chord; d) (i) two features (texture or structure; plus rhythm/tempo, dynamics, articulation, tonality or character) and (ii) describe a difference in key (relative major/minor).

comps: Marks

150 total: three accompanied songs 30 each (90), unaccompanied song 21, sight-singing 21, aural tests 18. Distinction 130-150, Merit 120-129, Pass 100-119 (a pass in each component is not required). UCAS points G6/G7/G8 (Pass/Merit/Distinction): 8/10/12, 12/14/16, 18/24/30.
Choosing pieces

Three accompanied songs from memory, one from each of Lists A, B and C, with live piano accompaniment (no recorded accompaniment; candidate cannot accompany themselves). One unaccompanied song from memory chosen from songs marked as eligible in any list (cannot also be sung accompanied; own choice of section, listed cuts need not be observed). Maximum one 'long' song among the accompanied songs. Any voice and key at G1-7; at G8 up to a tone above/below published keys. Songs complete including repeats unless the listing gives cuts; any edition may be used; any gender; original language or singing translation allowed. Song lists are the same as for Singing for Musical Theatre Performance Grades.
Before you enter
Grade 5 Music Theory (or Practical Musicianship Grade 5, or Grade 5 on a Practical Grades solo jazz instrument, or accepted alternative) required before entering Grade 6, 7 or 8. No Initial Grade.
Digital exams

Song lists are shared with the Performance Grades qualification (candidates taking both at the same grade are advised to prepare different songs); the text mentions face-to-face and digital exams generally but gives no separate digital requirements.
sections: Scales & technical work

No scales, arpeggios or technical work. Components: three accompanied songs, one unaccompanied song (1-2 min section, G1-5; 1-3 min, G6-8, chosen from songs marked as eligible), sight-singing, aural tests.
Sight-reading
Sight-singing (accompanied by examiner at piano, 30 seconds preparation): As Grade 6 plus 5/4 time, triplets, tempo changes and pause sign followed by a tempo.
Aural & other tests

a) sing the lower part of a two-part phrase; b) sing four intervals above (up to a 7th) or below (up to a 5th) a given note; c) identify a sung note in a chord (root, 3rd, 5th or 7th); d) (i) two features from rhythm/tempo, dynamics, articulation, tonality, character, texture, structure and (ii) describe a key difference (relative or tonic major/minor).

150 total: three accompanied songs 30 each (90), unaccompanied song 21, sight-singing 21, aural tests 18. Distinction 130-150, Merit 120-129, Pass 100-119 (a pass in each component is not required). UCAS points G6/G7/G8 (Pass/Merit/Distinction): 8/10/12, 12/14/16, 18/24/30.
Choosing pieces

Three accompanied songs from memory, one from each of Lists A, B and C, with live piano accompaniment (no recorded accompaniment; candidate cannot accompany themselves). One unaccompanied song from memory chosen from songs marked as eligible in any list (cannot also be sung accompanied; own choice of section, listed cuts need not be observed). Maximum one 'long' song among the accompanied songs. Any voice and key at G1-7; at G8 up to a tone above/below published keys. Songs complete including repeats unless the listing gives cuts; any edition may be used; any gender; original language or singing translation allowed. Song lists are the same as for Singing for Musical Theatre Performance Grades.
Before you enter
Grade 5 Music Theory (or Practical Musicianship Grade 5, or Grade 5 on a Practical Grades solo jazz instrument, or accepted alternative) required before entering Grade 6, 7 or 8. No Initial Grade.
Digital exams

Song lists are shared with the Performance Grades qualification (candidates taking both at the same grade are advised to prepare different songs); the text mentions face-to-face and digital exams generally but gives no separate digital requirements.
sections: Scales & technical work

No scales, arpeggios or technical work. Components: three accompanied songs, one unaccompanied song (1-2 min section, G1-5; 1-3 min, G6-8, chosen from songs marked as eligible), sight-singing, aural tests.
Sight-reading
Sight-singing (accompanied by examiner at piano, 30 seconds preparation): As Grade 7 plus octave intervals and a change of time signature.
Aural & other tests

a) sing the lowest part of a three-part phrase played twice; b) sing four intervals above/below different given notes (up to an octave, incl. aug.4th/dim.5th); c) identify a sung note in a chord (root, 3rd, 5th, 6th, 7th or 9th); d) (i) describe the characteristic features of a played piece and (ii) describe a key difference (relative/tonic major or minor, or up a semitone or tone).

exams.name: ARSM
exams.full: Associate of the Royal Schools of Music — ABRSM Level 4 Diploma in Music Performance
exams.syllabus: RQF Level 4 (EQF 5), about the end of the first year of an undergraduate course; 90 credits, 54 GLH, 900 TQT
comps: Entry requirement

A pass at Grade 8 on the same or a closely related instrument: ABRSM Practical or Performance Grade 8, or an accepted equivalent from another board (for example Trinity, LCM, MTB, Guildhall, RIAM, AMEB or UNISA). No theory prerequisite.
Format & marks

Face-to-face (public venue or private visit) OR digital (video recorded at a time and place of the candidate's choice, with no fixed sessions; video uploaded at booking or within 28 days). Performance only: 30-minute programme (±2 min), timed from the first note to the last. Marks: pieces 30 (60%) + performance as a whole 20 (40%) = 50. Distinction 45–50, Merit 40–44, Pass 34–39, Below Pass 17–33.
Programme rules

At least 20 minutes from the ARSM repertoire list for the instrument, plus up to 10 minutes of own-choice music at Grade 8 standard or above. No written or spoken elements and no other tests (no viva, no programme notes, no quick study). Candidates submit a programme form, or enter programme details online for digital exams.
sections: About the repertoire list

Official ARSM repertoire list for singing for musical theatre, read from the ABRSM PDF (64 entries). All songs may be sung by any voice or gender, with pronouns adjusted accordingly. Songs should be sung in the key specified, up to one tone higher or lower. Recorded accompaniments are not permitted. Own-choice music is also allowed within the programme rules above. Check the board's current list before entering; lists are updated online.
General notes

Pathway as of Oct 2026: ARSM (L4) → LRSM (L6) → FRSM (L7). DipABRSM is withdrawn (last date 31 Dec 2023). The old-format LRSM closed 30 Apr 2024 and the old FRSM closed 31 Oct 2024. All three current diplomas require only Grade 8 in the instrument (ABRSM or an equivalent board for LRSM/FRSM). No Grade 5 or 6 theory prerequisite is stated for any current performance diploma. Under the old syllabus, Grade 5 theory appeared only as a condition on some substitutions. ARSM has no written element. LRSM/FRSM need a written (2,000 / 3,500 words) or spoken-video (10 / 17 min) supporting-evidence submission. Digital exams have no fixed sessions: book, pay and upload any time; for digital ARSM the video goes in at booking or within 28 days. Specific LRSM/FRSM upload windows weren't stated in the spec, which refers to abrsm.org/how-to-book. ABRSM discontinued printed diploma syllabuses, and lists are updated online, so re-check the abrsm.org pages before entering. abrsm.org HTML pages returned redirect errors to the fetch tool, so some details come from the PDFs and ABRSM's Taiwan mirror.
General rules (all instruments)

Both LRSM and FRSM programmes must be balanced and varied: a variety of moods, keys and tempi and at least two pieces or movements contrasting by period or style. Works and movements must be played complete unless the repertoire list says otherwise, and any list-specific instructions must be followed. Music published with an accompaniment must be performed with one; any suitable instrument may accompany provided the candidate stays the main soloist, candidates arrange their own accompanist, and pre-recorded accompaniments are not allowed unless the composer intended them. Memory is not required (but encouraged if it helps). Any edition matching the list entry may be used and own-choice music must exist as a legible, fully notated score; performing from unauthorised photocopies of copyright editions is not allowed. Own-choice may include the candidate's own composition or arrangement but must still be at or above the required standard, and ABRSM cannot give prior approval of own-choice standard. An audience is encouraged but not required. Infringements (wrong length, too much own choice without approval, wrong movements, edited video) can bring a warning, mark deduction or disqualification. A video can only ever be submitted once, and the same Unit 2 work cannot be reused at a higher level.
